sources.note: Describes Part Two as 'a summary of phonology, noun classes and pronominal forms for each of the six languages. The phonology has very modest claims'; no prosodic detail.

sources.citation: Seligmann, Brenda Z. 1911. Note on the language of the Nubas of Southern Kordofan. Zeitschrift für Kolonialsprachen 1: 167-188.
sources.note: Only a transcription note, p.171: 'Long and short vowels are marked.. and stress is indicated by ´'. Eliri (=Nding, village Dayo) words in the comparative tables carry occasional acute marks; no statement of where stress falls. This is the sole primary data behind Meinhof's 1916-17 sketch.

sources.citation: Quint, Nicolas. 2020. Kordofanian. In R. Vossen & G. Dimmendaal (eds.), The Oxford Handbook of African Languages. Oxford: OUP (HAL halshs-03093501).
sources.note: Nding listed among nine Talodian languages; one lexical item cited; family-level 'probably all Kordofanian languages are tone languages'; nothing on stress.

sources.note: Secondhand data, no analysis: reproduces Schadeberg's 1981 110-item Nding (Liri) survey list (entries cite Schadeberg 1981: 19ff.) with his surface pitch marks re-notated (acute = high; grave added for Schadeberg's unmarked low; circumflex on several Nding forms, e.g. =bbik 'big', p=ulgak, akU), and states at group level that the Talodi languages' tonal systems 'usually involve two registers'. An open-access carrier of Schadeberg's tone-marked Nding forms (the 1981 survey itself is print-only and unobtained); no Nding-specific tonal analysis.
